result.summary: A high-density urban intersection with multi-lane roadways and significant pedestrian activity. The environment includes marked continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and wide sidewalks, but lacks physical traffic calming like curb extensions or refuge islands.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to multiple lanes of traffic for a significant duration without a mid-block refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk spanning the width of the intersection.

hazards.name: Turning vehicle conflicts
hazards.description: High-volume urban intersection where turning vehicles may fail to yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection where vehicles are visible.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at corners to shorten crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a high-density urban intersection with wide multi-lane roadways and high-visibility continental crosswalks. While pedestrian infrastructure like signals and sidewalks are present, the crossing distance remains significant across four lanes of traffic, including a dedicated bus lane.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Multiple-threat risk
hazards.description: Multiple travel lanes in the same direction can lead to one vehicle blocking the view of a pedestrian for another vehicle.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image shows a high-density urban intersection with wide sidewalks and signalized pedestrian crossings. While basic infrastructure like marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals are present, the multi-lane one-way street configuration creates a significant crossing distance for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Multi-lane One-way Traffic
hazards.description: The wide, one-way street layout can encourage higher vehicle speeds and create multiple-threat crash risks at the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway traveling away from the viewer

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: If lane widths allow, install a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: A high-density urban environment with wide sidewalks and a marked zebra crosswalk. The street features multiple travel lanes, including a dedicated bus lane, and is equipped with pedestrian signals and street lighting.
